issues.failure_explanation: Substituting $\delta_N=\varepsilon/(2\rho_N\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|)$ into the sample-size condition of Theorem \ref{OC theorem} gives $M\propto\gamma_N\max\{\|\bm{G}_N\|,\|\bm{T}_N\|\}\kappa(\bm{G}_N)(1+\|\bm{C}_N\|\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|)^2\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(\cdot)$. The display keeps only the term $\kappa(\bm{G}_N)\\|\bm{C}_N\|^2\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|^4$, which is smaller by the factor $\big(\|\bm{C}_N\|\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|/(1+\|\bm{C}_N\|\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|)\\big)^2$. Whenever $\|\bm{C}_N\|\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|<1$ (e.g. $\Aa=0$, or a well-conditioned basis with small $\bm{C}_N$) the display understates the sufficient sample size — with $\bm{C}_N=0$ it even asserts a vanishing requirement — so it is not a valid consequence of the theorem as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the display by $M=\mathcal{O}\big(\gamma_N\max\{\|\bm{G}_N\|,\|\bm{T}_N\|\}\kappa(\bm{G}_N)(1+\|\bm{C}_N\|\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|)^2\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|^2\log(\tfrac{N}{1-p})\varepsilon^{-2}\big)$, i.e. substitute $\delta_N$ into Theorem \ref{OC theorem} without dropping the lower-order terms.
issues.overall_effect: The general sample-complexity formula for approximating $\Aa_N$ is wrong in regimes with $\|\bm{C}_N\|\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|<1$; the two cost examples built on it assume bounded $\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|,\|\bm{C}_N\|$ or $\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|\sim N^{1/2}$, i.e. the regime where the simplification is valid, so they are unaffected.
issues.title: Order-of-convergence display understates the sufficient sample size
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the display restores the exact consequence of the theorem; all substantive claims, rates, and the examples built on it survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The noisy Gram matrix satisfies $\E[\tl{\bm{G}}_{NM}]=\bm{G}_N+\E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger]\neq\bm{G}_N$ (errors-in-variables bias), and the noisy second moment of the operator samples is $\bm{T}_N+\E[\bm{\xi}\bm{\xi}^\dagger]$. In the proof, $\bm{G}_N,\bm{T}_N,\bm{C}_N$ are silently redefined as the corresponding noisy moments (and \eqref{gcdef}/\eqref{sum def} even use $\bm{\eta}_N^m$ in place of $\bm{\xi}_N^m$ in $\bm{c}_m$), so the Bernstein/Neumann argument controls the distance to the biased limit operator with matrix $\bm{C}_N(\bm{G}_N+\E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger])^{-1}$, not to the true Galerkin projection $\Aa_N$. Since $\tl{\Aa}_{NM}$ converges to that biased operator, $\|\tl{\Aa}_{NM}-\Aa_N\|$ cannot be made arbitrarily small: for $\delta$ (equivalently $\varepsilon$) below the bias floor the claimed probability bound is false. No assumption in the paper controls $\|\E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger]\|$ or $\|\E[\bm{\xi}\bm{\xi}^\dagger]\|$ relative to $\bm{G}_N,\bm{T}_N$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either debias the Gram matrix (e.g. subtract the noise covariance, requiring a new known-covariance hypothesis) or redefine the target as the biased operator with matrix $\bm{C}_N(\bm{G}_N+\E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger])^{-1}$ and add the resulting bias $\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa(\bm{G}_N)}\|\bm{C}_N\|\|\bm{G}_N^{-1}\|^2\|\E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger]\|$ to every noise bound. Either way the advertised guarantee of arbitrary accuracy for $\Aa_N$ is lost.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition \ref{noise bound} is false as stated; Theorem \ref{OC theorem noise}, which claims $\mathbb{P}[\|\tl{\Aa}_{NM}-\Aa_N\|\le\varepsilon]\ge p$ for arbitrary $\varepsilon\in(0,\rho_N)$, is false; the 'order of convergence with noise' display and the advertised consistency of the approximation under measurement noise fail.
issues.title: Noisy Gram matrix is biased; the noise error bounds claim false consistency
issues.why_classification: The estimator is inconsistent for the true target because the bias $\E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger]$ is uncontrolled by any hypothesis; every noise-section bound and the paper's advertised convergence under noise fail, and no comparable version of the claims survives without a new debiasing construction or a redefined target with a bias floor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists $\gamma_N^{}$ such that $\mu$ almost everywhere $\abs{{\Psi}_N(\bm{x})|^2< \gamma_N^{}$

issues.failure_explanation: On the truncation event, $|\bm{g}_m|^2=|\Psi_N(\bm{x}_m)+\bm{\eta}_N^m|^2\le2|\Psi_N|^2+2|\bm{\eta}_N^m|^2\le2\gamma_N+2\tl{\gamma}_N$ (approached with equality in the collinear case $|\Psi_N|^2=\gamma_N$, $|\bm{\eta}_N^m|^2=\tl{\gamma}_N$), not $\gamma_N+\tl{\gamma}_N$ as claimed. Hence the almost-sure boundedness hypothesis $|\bm{c}|^2,|\bm{g}|^2\le\gamma$ of Corollary \ref{Bernstein Lemma} is not verified with $\gamma=\gamma_N+\tl{\gamma}_N$; the valid choice is $\gamma=2(\gamma_N+\tl{\gamma}_N)$, which doubles the required sample size in the proposition and in Theorem \ref{OC theorem noise}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use $|\Psi+\eta|^2\le2(\gamma_N+\tl{\gamma}_N)$ in \eqref{bernbound} and replace $\gamma_N+\tl{\gamma}_N$ by $2(\gamma_N+\tl{\gamma}_N)$ in the sample-size conditions of Proposition \ref{noise bound} and Theorem \ref{OC theorem noise} (doubling the required $M$).
issues.overall_effect: The sufficient sample size in Proposition \ref{noise bound} and Theorem \ref{OC theorem noise} is understated by a factor of 2, so the stated probability guarantees do not follow for the stated $M$.
issues.title: Bernstein boundedness condition in the noise proof is off by a factor of 2
issues.why_classification: A short local correction (doubling the boundedness constant and the resulting sample size) restores the argument with no loss of content or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: With $(\bm{\eta}_N,\bm{\xi}_N)\\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2\Id_{2N})$, the event $\{|\bm{\eta}_N|^2+|\bm{\xi}_N|^2\le\tl{\gamma}_N\}$ has probability $F_{2N}(\tl{\gamma}_N/\sigma^2)$, since $|\bm{\eta}_N|^2+|\bm{\xi}_N|^2\sim\sigma^2\chi_{2N}^2$ — the sum of two independent $\chi_N^2$ variables — not $1-F_N(\gamma_N)$ as computed; the computation treats only one of the two $N$-dimensional noise vectors. For $\gamma_N=2N$ and $\tl{\gamma}_N=\sigma^2\gamma_N$ one gets $\tl{p}_N=\mathbb{P}[\chi_{2N}^2\le2N]\approx1/2$, far from the claimed $\ge1-(2/e)^{N/2}\approx1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take $\tl{\gamma}_N=2\sigma^2\gamma_N$ (equivalently, recompute the tail bound with $2N$ degrees of freedom), which restores a $\tl{p}_N\ge1-(2/e)^{N}$-type estimate.
issues.overall_effect: With the stated truncation level, $\tl{p}_N\approx1/2$, so Theorem \ref{OC theorem noise} is applicable only for $p<1/2$ as computed; the example's qualitative conclusion that the noise has small effect on the bound survives after correction.
issues.title: Noise example computes the truncation probability with the wrong chi-square degrees of freedom
issues.why_classification: Enlarging the truncation level (or correcting the degrees of freedom) is a contained one-line repair that leaves the example's qualitative conclusion and the applicability of the noise theorem intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, if $\psi \in {\Ff}$ is continuous almost everywhere, we can view it as an element of $\wh{\Ff}_M$ through the (non-injective) mapping

Suppose Assumptions \ref{assumption} and \ref{moments assumption} hold, then there exists an $\mathbb{N}$-valued random variable $m_0$ such that $\wh{\Psi}\subset\wh{\Ff}_M$ are almost surely linearly independent for all $M\ge m_0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The normalization $\|f_M\|_\Dd=1$ presupposes an identification of $\wh{\Ff}_{NM}$ with $\Ff_N$, which exists only when $\wh{\bm{G}}_{NM}$ is invertible (the identification is non-injective otherwise, and Lemma \ref{invertiblelemma} guarantees invertibility only under Assumptions \ref{assumption} and \ref{moments assumption} and only for $M\ge m_0$). Under the theorem's sole hypothesis (Assumption \ref{continuous}) this can fail for every $M$ — e.g. if $\mu$ is supported on a single point, $\wh{\Ff}_M$ is one-dimensional for all $M$ — so the normalized eigenpairs in the statement are not well-defined; moreover, without moment bounds the empirical averages $\frac1M\sum_m|\Aa\psi(\bm{x}_m)|^2$ can diverge, so the eigenvalue sequence need not be bounded and the claimed convergent subsequence is not ensured.

failure_location.quote: Suppose $\Psi$ satisfies Assumption \ref{continuous} and let $({\lambda}_{M}, f_{M})$ be a sequence of eigenvalue and normalised eigenfunction pairs of $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$, i.e., $\norm{f_{M}}_{\Dd}=1, \wh{\Aa}_{NM} f_{M}=\lambda_Mf_{M}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume Assumptions \ref{assumption} and \ref{moments assumption} in the first part (or index the sequence by $M\ge m_0$ as in Lemma \ref{invertiblelemma}); the boundedness of the eigenvalues then follows from the moment bounds and the conclusion holds.
issues.overall_effect: The first part of Theorem \ref{convergence eigenfunctions data theorem} is not well-posed under its stated hypothesis, and neither is the analogous first part of Theorem \ref{convergence eigenfunctions joint theorem}, which assumes the same single hypothesis; the second parts, which carry the full assumptions, are unaffected.
issues.title: Normalized eigenpairs in the data-limit eigensystem theorem are not well-defined under the stated hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypotheses (or starting the sequence at $m_0$) is a local hypothesis repair that makes the statement well-posed and the conclusion valid, with no loss of method, scope, or rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose there exists a sequence $(\lambda_N, f_N)$ of eigenvalue and normalized eigenfunction pairs of $\Aa_N$, i.e., $\norm{f_N}_{\Dd}=1, \Aa_N f_N=\lambda_Nf_N$.

A direct consequence of the above definitions is that $
orm{f}_{\Ff}\leq 
orm{f}_{\Dd}$ and $\Aa\colon\Dd	o\Ff$ is a continuous operator with $
orm{\Aa}\leq 1$.
In many cases, however, $\Aa$ will \emph{not} be bounded (for example, if $\Aa$ is the generator $\Ll$ of the Koopman operator).

issues.failure_explanation: Each $\Aa_N$ is bounded because $\Ff_N$ is finite-dimensional, but the norms $\|\Aa_N\|_{\Ff_N\to\Ff_N}$ need not be bounded in $N$ when $\Aa$ is unbounded: $|\lambda_N|=\|\Aa_Nf_N\|_\Ff/\|f_N\|_\Ff\le1/\|f_N\|_\Ff$ (using $\|\Aa_Nf_N\|_\Ff\le\|\Aa f_N\|_\Ff\le\|f_N\|_\Dd=1$), and $\|f_N\|_\Ff$ can tend to $0$. Concretely, for $\Aa$ the Koopman generator (a second-order operator, the paper's central example) with a piecewise linear FEM dictionary — or even a Fourier basis — $\Aa_N$ is a discrete Laplacian-type matrix whose eigenvalues have magnitude $\sim N^2$; choosing $(\lambda_N,f_N)$ as the corresponding $\Dd$-normalized eigenpairs gives $|\lambda_N|\to\infty$, so no subsequence with convergent eigenvalues exists and the theorem is false as stated. The proof's inference 'for each $N$, $\Aa_N$ is bounded, thus $(\lambda_N)$ is bounded' conflates per-$N$ boundedness with a uniform bound.

failure_location.quote: Additionally, for each $N$, $\Aa_N$ is bounded. Thus, the sequence of eigenvalues $(\lambda_{N})$ is also bounded and has a convergent subsequence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict $\Aa$ to be bounded on $\Ff$, or impose a uniform bound on $\|\Aa_N\|_{\Ff_N\to\Ff_N}$ with $\Ff$-normalized eigenvectors (both exclude the generator case that motivates the paper), or re-prove spectral convergence via resolvent/spectral-projection arguments for unbounded operators.
issues.overall_effect: The dictionary-limit spectral convergence theorem fails in exactly the advertised regime (unbounded generators); the joint-limit eigensystem theorem, whose first part rests on the same false boundedness claim, fails with it, and the paper's advertised spectral convergence for EDMD/gEDMD-type approximations of generators is lost.
issues.title: Eigenvalues of the Galerkin projection are unbounded for unbounded operators; the subsequence-convergence theorem is false
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false in the paper's central target setting — discretizations of the Koopman generator have $\Aa_N$-eigenvalues of size $\sim N^2$ — and every repair either abandons the unbounded-operator regime or requires an essentially new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption \ref{projection assumption} gives $\|(\rm{Id}-\Pp_{\Ff_N})\phi\|_\Ff\to0$ for each fixed $\phi\in\Ff$, not for the varying sequence $\Aa f_{N_i}$; in general $\|(\rm{Id}-\Pp_{\Ff_N})\Aa f_N\|_\Ff$ does not vanish (for the Koopman operator of a rotation with Fourier subspaces and eigenvectors with $\lambda_N\to0$, one computes $\|(\rm{Id}-\Pp_N)\Aa f_N\|_\Ff=\sqrt{1-\lambda_N^2}\to1$). The inner-product limit the proof needs is nevertheless correct via $\br{(\rm{Id}-\Pp_{N_i})\Aa f_{N_i},g}_\Ff=\br{\Aa f_{N_i},(\rm{Id}-\Pp_{N_i})g}_\Ff\to0$, using $\|\Aa f_{N_i}\|_\Ff\le\|f_{N_i}\|_\Dd=1$ and the assumption applied to the fixed test function $g$; so this is a false intermediate claim with a one-line repair, not a false conclusion.

failure_location.quote: in the second we used that $(\rm{Id}-\Pp_{\Ff_{N_i}})\Aa f_{N_i}\to 0$ by Assumption \ref{projection assumption}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Justify the limit by $\br{(\rm{Id}-\Pp_{\Ff_{N_i}})\Aa f_{N_i},g}_\Ff=\br{\Aa f_{N_i},(\rm{Id}-\Pp_{\Ff_{N_i}})g}_\Ff\to0$, using $\|\Aa f_{N_i}\|_\Ff\le\|f_{N_i}\|_\Dd=1$ and Assumption \ref{projection assumption} applied to the fixed vector $g$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the second part of Theorem \ref{convergence eigenfunctions dictionary theorem} contains a false intermediate claim; the conclusion remains correct after a one-line repair, but the proof as written is invalid.
issues.title: Projection error on a varying sequence is claimed to vanish; the cited assumption does not give this
issues.why_classification: The stated justification is invalid and the intermediate norm claim is false in general, but the needed limit follows from a short adjointness argument, so the conclusion is fully preserved by a local repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $({\lambda}_{N M}, f_{N M})_{(N,M)\in\N^2} $ be a sequence of eigenvalue and normalized eigenfunction pairs of $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$

issues.failure_explanation: The sequence $(\lambda_{NM},f_{NM})$ is an arbitrary selection of one eigenpair per $(N,M)$, so convergence along the subsequence $(N_i,M_{N_i})$ does not constrain the selected pairs at larger sample sizes: if $\Aa_N$ has eigenvalues tending to $1$ and $-1$, choosing $\lambda_{NM}$ according to the parity of $M$ yields $\lambda_{N_iM_{N_i}}\to1$ along even $M_{N_i}$ but $\lambda_{N_i(M_{N_i}+1)}\to-1$. The clause 'for any sequence $M'_{N_i}\ge M_{N_i}$' is therefore false for a general selection, independently of the eigenvalue-boundedness failure (ISSUE-006). (The second part of the proof also justifies a limit 'because $\Aa$ is bounded', which is false for generators, though the conclusion follows from weak convergence and $\Aa^*g\in\Ff$.)

failure_location.quote: such that, for any sequence $M'_{N_i} \geq M_{N_i}$, almost surely $\lambda_{N_iM'_{N_i}}\to\lambda, \quad f_{N_iM'_{N_i}} \stackrel{w}{\to} f,\quad\text{when $N_i\to\infty$}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the clause 'for any sequence $M'_{N_i}\ge M_{N_i}$' (retaining convergence of the chosen subsequence), or specify a deterministic selection rule for the eigenpairs for which the extension is meaningful.
issues.overall_effect: The first part of Theorem \ref{convergence eigenfunctions joint theorem} remains unjustified even if the eigenvalue-boundedness problem is repaired; only plain subsequence convergence of the chosen eigenpairs is supportable.
issues.title: Joint-limit eigensystem theorem claims convergence along every larger sample size for an arbitrary eigenpair selection
issues.why_classification: Dropping or qualifying the overbroad quantifier clause is a local repair that leaves the main subsequence-convergence claim unchanged.
